approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates neural proposals with two graph refinement phases, learns from exact accepted molecular trajectories using rank-weighted trajectory balance and a joint normalizer, and regularizes the adapting policy toward a frozen corpus-trained prior. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior chooses graph offspring for evaluation while preserving the first fresh-policy handoff. The reusable prior is selected along unchanged unlabeled training by valid, connected, unique generation yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. During a neural phase the current sampler uses only the adapted policy distribution; the frozen reference influences learning but does not directly participate in token selection.
approach.novelty: Anchor each neural token draw to the frozen reference by using the normalized geometric mean of the adapted-policy and prior probabilities at the same generated prefix. This keeps both the learned score preference and the reference in the actual sampling distribution. The earlier children changed prior preparation, replay allocation, KL direction or trajectory-balance credit; this one preserves the Parent learning stack and changes only ancestral generation. Lower reference divergence is tested directly on the sampled prefixes, while novel molecular yield, graph-feedback transfer and endpoint score remain separate empirical questions.

observed_bottleneck: The current Parent n-dd7b8aa31113 samples neural tokens directly from its adapted policy even after accepted-score updates move conditional probabilities away from the fixed prior. Its complete mean is 0.5501977216134929 with SD 0.02173839408580094. Only 8156 of 12000 raw online draws are valid terminated molecules, including 1079/1200 in the first policy batches and 7077/10800 later. The first batches already follow initial-score adaptation; these are not pure-prior assays. Its independently sampled preparation diagnostic produced 705 valid unique molecules of 768 draws from the selected priors, a different distribution and opportunity set. The reference direction sibling n-dc38d4efbf01 executed its restoring gradients but both measured divergence and total variation increased after learning in every session, and mean score fell by 0.006384. The centered-credit sibling n-f5cfa75eff1c increased unresolved common error, reduced valid-novel yield to 6861/12280 and reduced later graph-family emission, with mean score lower by 0.007543. These findings leave a concrete generation behavior to test: ancestral sampling has no direct reference anchoring at the actual generated prefix. They do not prove that prior divergence causes invalid chemistry or that anchoring will improve endpoint search.
hypothesis: Generate neural proposals ancestrally from the normalized geometric mean of the adapted-policy and frozen-prior next-token distributions at each shared generated prefix, with equal fixed exponents and unchanged accepted-score learning.

finding_summary.headline: Geometric anchoring improved valid-novel yield but weakened neural scores and missed the mean-score gain
finding_summary.insights: Direct reference anchoring can substantially improve syntactic and novelty yield at generated prefixes while attenuating useful accepted-score adaptation. The effect was strongest after the first adapted-policy batch: later valid-novel yield rose from 64.00% to 85.42%, while later accepted neural mean score fell from 0.211885 to 0.160124. Graph feedback continued to train the policy: all 6,480 nonterminal graph-bearing replay steps had nonzero graph-only gradients, and exact accepted graph log likelihood increased by 0.180643 on average per training exposure. The weaker downstream family overlap and scores therefore occurred despite active graph learning. Ring-core overlap is a descriptive connection, not proof of causal or functional transfer. The extra raw yield did not expand the evaluated neural stream under this sampler. Both runs emitted exactly 1,500 neural molecules from 150 calls and needed no additional sampling call. The valid surplus discarded after filling a batch increased from 6,491 to 8,819. Mean active sequence length shortened from 59.409 to 48.290 draws including EOS, but measured neural-phase generation time rose from 14.608 to 27.896 seconds across the runs, including diagnostic overhead. This narrows the result: improved parser/novelty yield alone was not a limiting resource for these full batches. The supplied chemistry assessment describes broad ring-rich output with ordinary medicinal motifs alongside reactive bonds, unusual heteroatom bonding, uncontrolled growth and absent stereochemical specification. Those combined neural/graph outputs do not establish that the extra unscored valid draws preserve useful functional context. The experiment supports the conditional distribution effect and higher raw yield, while leaving useful molecular transfer and search advantage unsupported. It does not show that the adapted weights stayed closer to the prior; the KL comparison holds the generated prefix fixed and compares two sampling distributions at that prefix.
finding_summary.results: The intended sampling mechanism activated. Across 12,000 raw neural sequences and 579,478 active token prefixes, the recorded behavior distribution differed from the adapted policy. On those same prefixes, mean KL divergence to the frozen prior fell from 0.182477 for the adapted-policy endpoint to 0.040980 for behavior; mean behavior/policy L1 distance was 0.144892. Every raw sequence had lower average behavior-to-prior divergence. All 150 saved audit prefixes reconstruct the registered geometric midpoint. Valid-novel raw yield rose from 7,991/12,000 (66.59%) to 10,319/12,000 (85.99%), improving in all three seeds and all five tasks. Invalid draws fell from 3,807 to 1,680, unterminated draws from 37 to zero and duplicates from 165 to one. However, mean accepted neural score fell from 0.204941 to 0.158382. Among 1,350 later neural emissions, exact ring-core overlap with previously trained graph molecules fell from 53 to 39. The three-seed mean final-best score was 0.542371 versus the parent's 0.550198, a paired change of -0.007826; population standard deviations were 0.030347 and 0.021738. Paired macro changes were +0.009185, -0.078386 and +0.045722. Task-mean changes were -0.020870 for zaleplon, -0.052561 for scaffold hopping, -0.012984 for DRD2, -0.004175 for median similarity and +0.051459 for sitagliptin. Every task completed all 300 evaluations.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal motifs coexist with reactive bonds, difficult polycycles and absent stereochemical specification.
molecular.overall_character: The evaluated proposals cover aromatic ethers, azaheterocycles, amines, amides, sulfones, fluorinated heterocycles and densely fused or bridged rings. Each task digest contains 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Across the task digests, ring-closure rates run from 0.9747 to 0.9966 and aromatic-presence rates from 0.9448 to 0.9839; these are fractions of proposal SMILES containing the relevant text, not ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. Mean SMILES lengths range from 43.7 to 65.4, with some much larger assemblies. Every stereocentre_rate is 0.0, despite structures with stereogenic ring junctions and substituted saturated atoms. The overall chemical vocabulary is broad, while the digest high-scoring sets repeatedly concentrate in particular scaffold families and seeds. Ordinary medicinal functional groups coexist with peroxides, terminal imines, unusual sulfur bonding, phosphines, N-fluorinated rings and small strained heterocycles. Compared with Parent n-dd7b8aa31113, the prominent families change, but neither chemical plausibility nor stereochemical completeness is consistently established. These are assessments of the evaluated molecular outputs; their trajectory source labels do not separate neural proposals from graph descendants, and they do not establish raw-generation validity or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest digest family consists of moderately sized pyridine/phenyl aromatic assemblies joined by a biaryl bond and a benzyl ether, with ethoxy or methoxy substituents and frequent halogens. CCOc1ccc(-c2ccccc2COc2cc(Cl)ccn2)cn1 has recognizable aryl-ether chemistry, aromatic nitrogen acceptors and no strongly basic aliphatic amine or carbonyl. Some close relatives add an amino group or close additional rings. Other seeds also explore substituted indole carboxamides and more elaborate fused heterocycles. The low end includes very large polyamide/polyamine assemblies, polyhydroxylated carbohydrate-like structures and a long-chain phosphorus/quaternary-ammonium/silicon compound. The optimizer ring-closure rate is 0.9885, aromatic-presence rate 0.9759 and mean SMILES length 43.7. The leading ether structures appear substantially more synthetically conventional than the oversized and unusually fused excursions.
liabilities: Aromatic-heavy structures and peripheral halogen/linker edits dominate the leading family; the output does not establish solubility, conformational preference or a synthesis route.
Large fragment combinations add long chains, numerous polar groups or unusual phosphorus/silicon/charge combinations while losing the favorable score range.
missing_features: The low-scoring large structures fail to retain the economical aromatic/acceptor arrangement and limited side-chain size seen in the stronger ether family.
The leading family shows little saturated stereodefined shape variation; whether such alternatives would improve this objective is unmeasured, rather than an established requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest spans 0.0 to 0.475614712250357, with median 0.151051. The leading aromatic ether scores 0.475614712250357, whereas the long-chain charged phosphorus/silicon structure scores 0.0 and the large polyamine/amide assembly scores 2.5085649778800826e-59. A close local comparison changes only ethoxy to propoxy on the chlorinated biaryl ether: 0.46457806514522626 becomes 0.3189563030428961. This supports a preference for a specific modest-size substitution pattern rather than indiscriminate chain growth. In the matched Parent seed-2 trajectory, the best molecule was a carbonyl- and nitrile-bearing bicyclic nitrogen scaffold at 0.46457806514522626; the Child seed-2 ether family reaches 0.475614712250357. Different functional-group families can therefore occupy a similar score range, and these data do not establish an obligatory missing amide, nitrile or particular unseen pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The leading digest family is a medium-to-large aromatic anilino-thienopyrimidine series, bearing phenyl or heteroaryl substituents, methoxy, methyl and halogens. Its ring nitrogens and anilino NH provide an organized acceptor/donor pattern, but many leading members also contain a terminal methylene imine or an aryl methyl peroxide. The simpler aryloxy members have familiar medicinal-chemistry connectivity. Other seeds develop much larger fused azaaromatic, urea/formamide and repeated polycyclic assemblies, including the long final seed-2 molecule cited here. The low end instead includes cyclic sulfones, sulfonamides, acids and flexible sulfone-linked aromatic structures. Ring-closure rate is 0.9908, aromatic-presence rate 0.9839 and mean SMILES length 65.4; the maximum is 187 characters. The scaffold vocabulary is plausible, but the peroxide/imine substitutions and complex final assemblies make overall synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: The terminal methylene imines and explicit O-O bonds deserve chemical stability and synthetic scrutiny; no such verification accompanies their scores.
Large fused and repeated azaaromatic assemblies accumulate difficult ring connections and densely substituted nitrogen chemistry without a correspondingly decisive score advantage.
missing_features: The weaker cyclic-sulfone and flexible-chain proposals lack the organized fused azaaromatic/anilino donor-acceptor context shared by the stronger Child family.

Chemically conventional substituent alternatives are not comparably developed across the leading family: high-scoring termini often become imines or peroxides. Their chemical replacement is a quality gap; an objective-score benefit is not established.

The leading Child digest does not reproduce the Parent high-scoring quinazoline/piperazinone arrangement, so the observed family coverage is incomplete rather than demonstrably missing one required atom or group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading imine-bearing anilino-thienopyrimidine scores 0.6720445459737293; its otherwise matching pendant phenyl analogue without fluorine scores 0.6441828361070634. The peroxide analogue scores 0.629303689979929, and a conventional phenoxy analogue scores 0.6254953764861295. Thus high scores coexist with both conventional and chemically concerning substituents; the small numerical differences do not prove the concerning groups are necessary. The cyclic sulfone/carboxylic acid at the low end scores 0.2596495291029798, whereas a very large final azaaromatic assembly still scores 0.594488188976378. The observed gradient emphasizes the particular aromatic nitrogen-rich context more clearly than it enforces simplicity or ordinary peripheral chemistry. Parent seed-1 reached 0.8301591128254581 in a quinazoline/piperazinone-rich family, while Child seed-1 reaches 0.6720445459737293 in the thienopyrimidine series. This is a change in explored high-scoring chemistry, not evidence that adding a particular parent fragment would reproduce its score.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecules combine hydrophobic chlorinated aromatic groups with accessible aliphatic amines. They include a flexible aminated tertiary organophosphine, dichlorophenylpiperazines with alkyl chains and unusual C=S(=O) sulfur centers, and larger fused heteroaromatic/aryl amine structures. The seed-2 family combines an arylpiperazine, a secondary amine linker, an aminophenol ring and a halogenated fused heterocycle. These are recognizably amine-rich rather than nitrogen-deficient outputs. The low end instead contains acylated/sulfonylated nitrogens, nitro hydrazones and neutral carbonyl-rich aromatics without the same exposed aliphatic amine context. Ring-closure rate is 0.9747, aromatic-presence rate 0.9448, halogen rate 0.7241 and mean SMILES length 47.9. The charged rate of 0.0126 concerns written formal charges and does not measure how often the neutral amines could protonate.
liabilities: The aminophosphines and C=S(=O)-bearing sulfur structures require more chemical justification than an accepted score provides. Long flexible alkyl branches and alkyl chlorides add further chemical liabilities.
Small N-N ring closures can radically change strain, basicity and geometry. A formal parser-accepted ring does not establish that the intended cyclic-amine chemistry has been preserved.
missing_features: The low-scoring carbonyl/sulfonyl-rich structures lack the exposed non-amide aliphatic amine context present in the strongest molecules; the generator as a whole clearly can produce that context.

Reliable preservation of favorable cyclic-amine topology is missing: the close piperazine-to-small-N-N-ring comparison loses the stronger score despite retaining the surrounding aryl and linker features.
Explicit configurations are absent at substituted saturated centers and ring junctions; no stereochemical preference can be inferred from these unassigned SMILES.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminophosphine scores 0.9957613133842727 and the sulfur-bearing arylpiperazine 0.9941946146870084, while the acylated/sulfonylated nitrogen structure scores 3.8021829379963674e-05. This supports accessible aliphatic amine plus hydrophobic aromatic context within the sampled structures, without identifying a binding pose or proving a contribution from phosphorus or unusual sulfur. A particularly informative pair preserves the rest of the seed-2 scaffold: its piperazine-containing molecule scores 0.9889622948332054, but contraction to the small N-N-containing ring in the final digest scores 0.4586415097801264. Correct local ring connectivity and amine spacing matter more than merely retaining nitrogen atoms. The Parent also produced arylpiperazines and bridged basic amines; its seed-2 arylpiperazine reached 0.9999999657062248 without the Child seed-0 phosphine or unusual sulfur motif. Those motifs are therefore not established as missing requirements.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains fairly large but compact multicyclic indole-containing scaffolds with fused/bridged saturated or unsaturated ketone rings and an aryl sulfone or sulfonamide linked to benzodioxole. This provides aromatic surface, an indole NH, carbonyl and sulfonyl acceptors, and substantial rigid three-dimensional connectivity, but the saturated stereogenic centers are unspecified. Other seeds explore nitrogen-rich fused systems with piperazine and xanthone-like aromatic carbonyl/ether frameworks carrying amines or amides. The final xanthone-like examples are more conventional than the most elaborate bridged indole structures. The low end ranges from ethane and butane to small imine/guanidine-like compounds and a sulfur-rich heterocycle. Ring-closure rate is 0.9966, aromatic-presence rate 0.9747 and mean SMILES length 56.0. Ring chemistry is abundant; the principal limitation is the plausibility and specification of the particular connectivity.
liabilities: Dense ring fusion and substituted ring junctions impose substantial synthetic and stereochemical demands that the SMILES and scores do not resolve.
Some nearby variants introduce N-N or N-O linkages, while a final example duplicates a large aromatic carbonyl framework. These changes add chemical complexity without establishing a stronger score.
missing_features: The low-end small compounds lack the connected aromatic and carbonyl-containing ring framework seen in the stronger examples; simply supplying nitrogen or a heterocycle does not reproduce that context.
The leading bridged structures lack explicit relative and absolute stereochemistry, leaving their chemically realizable three-dimensional form underspecified.
The data do not identify a further obligatory functional group: different Parent and Child ring/carbonyl arrangements reach similar score ranges.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading saturated ketone/indole/aryl-sulfone molecule scores 0.26804278537408394, compared with 0.25552813151632275 for its close unsaturated ketone counterpart and 0.24018374019946398 for the corresponding unsaturated sulfonamide connection. These comparisons favor particular local saturation and linkage choices within an already rich ring scaffold, rather than ring count alone. Ethane scores 0.012461119656980673 and the small acyclic imine-rich compound 0.014440527314146958; neither carries the aromatic-carbonyl spatial context of the stronger families. A final aminomethylpiperazine/xanthone-like molecule scores 0.21967074064860953. Parent seed-1 reached 0.26493557493264663 with a different benzofused diazepinone/benzodioxole/sulfonylpiperazine arrangement. The Child dense indole polycycle is consequently one observed solution family, not an established necessary scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family is moderately sized and fluorinated, combining an aromatic oxadiazole, an unsaturated ring containing adjacent nitrogens, a partly unsaturated nitrogen- or sulfur-containing ring and a short alcohol side chain. The top nitrogen-ring structures include N-F bonds as well as carbon-bound fluorine/fluoromethyl substituents. Several sulfur analogues instead have the unusual explicit C=[SH] connectivity. A different high-scoring seed-0 structure combines a fluorinated unsaturated chain, pyridyl sulfonamide and small fused N/O rings. Low-scoring structures include long-chain cations, polyhydroxylated carbohydrate-like molecules, peptide-like expansions and repeated copies of the leading scaffold. Ring-closure rate is 0.9943, aromatic-presence rate 0.9644 and mean SMILES length 45.1. The proposal charged rate is 0.2264, although the leading fluorinated family is formally neutral. The structures show chemical variety but weak assurance that their unusual heteroatom bonds and ring geometry correspond to tractable, stable compounds.
liabilities: N-F bonds, adjacent nitrogen connectivity, unusual C=[SH] centers and the small fused N/O ring example require direct chemical scrutiny. Their scores alone provide no stability or synthetic evidence.
Repeated-scaffold growth and long-chain/polyfunctional excursions can destroy the observed favorable size/composition balance even while retaining recognizable substructures.
missing_features: Oversized and heavily hydroxylated proposals fail to preserve the modest-size fluorinated heterocycle/alcohol arrangement associated with the stronger Child structures.

Chemically conventional counterparts that retain the leading family's size, atom spacing and heteroaromatic context are not well established; the strongest examples instead contain N-fluorinated or unusual sulfur-containing rings. This is a plausibility gap, with any score benefit of replacement unproven.
Explicit stereochemical definition is absent despite substituted saturated ring atoms and multiple possible configurations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading N-fluorinated compound scores 0.5728383251386864, with the closely related direct ring-fluorine analogue at 0.5544223426906131. A matched change shortens the latter molecule's hydroxyethyl substituent to hydroxymethyl, giving the final molecule at 0.25315061544485684. The local placement of fluorinated groups and alcohol-bearing carbon spacing therefore matters in this family. A much enlarged repeated-family molecule scores 1.5864369562081132e-30, and the cited polyhydroxylated carbohydrate-like structure scores 0.0. This is a strong observed size/composition constraint, not a general reward for accumulating heteroatoms. Parent seed-2 reached 0.3246833344580741 with a fluorovinyl-urea and indole-containing nitrogen heterocycle; the Child reaches its different fluorinated-ring family at 0.5728383251386864. The observed chemical change does not establish that N-F or unusual sulfur bonding is needed, and the trajectories do not reveal a unique missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring digest molecules contain aryl methyl peroxides, terminal methylene imines, aminophosphines, C=S(=O) sulfur centers and N-fluorinated rings. Conventional aryl ethers and cyclic amines also occur among strong molecules, so unusual bonding is not the only observed route to useful chemical context.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish a chemically credible functional group from a locally acceptable heteroatom or bond replacement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent or validate complete bonded functional-group neighborhoods during generation and edits. Support chemically credible alternatives that retain local size, donor/acceptor arrangement and attachment geometry; do not use a high score as evidence that an unusual bond pattern is chemically sound.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A digest pair keeps the same surrounding aromatic scaffold and linker but changes a piperazine into a small N-N-containing ring, with observed scores 0.9889622948332054 and 0.4586415097801264. Another close pair changes hydroxyethyl to hydroxymethyl and has scores 0.5544223426906131 and 0.25315061544485684. Atom inventory alone misses these differences.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful cyclic-amine topology and local atom spacing are not reliably retained when related molecules are generated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve chemically meaningful ring neighborhoods and attachment distances when varying peripheral groups, and explore ring-size or linker changes as explicit coherent alternatives. The generator should be able to vary substituents without inadvertently reconstructing the central functional group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A chlorinated aromatic ether scores 0.46457806514522626 with ethoxy but 0.3189563030428961 with propoxy. A fluorinated heterocycle at 0.5728383251386864 contrasts with an enlarged repeated-family structure at 1.5864369562081132e-30. Large nitrogen-rich aromatic assemblies also remain visible among final proposals; the longest proposal SMILES in the digest is 187 characters.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain compact molecular context when combining or extending existing structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded growth, deletion and fragment replacement that preserve useful neighborhoods and permit exploration at comparable molecular size. Avoid treating fragment duplication or appended chemical content as a substitute for a coherent new scaffold; accepted scores should determine which size regime remains useful.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited molecules nevertheless contain substituted saturated amine rings, fluorinated ring carbons and dense bridged or fused ring junctions. The output therefore describes connectivity families without resolving their stereochemical molecular identities.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated structures do not specify stereochemistry even when the depicted topology creates stereogenic centers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve existing stereochemical information and provide chemically consistent stereoisomer generation for newly created centers and ring junctions. Treat the absence of stereochemical testing as uncertainty; these trajectories do not establish which configuration, if any, would receive a stronger score.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.
